standard_prerequisites.name: Flat morphism of ringed topoi
standard_prerequisites.statement: A morphism of ringed topoi is flat when its structure sheaf is flat as a sheaf of modules over the inverse image of the structure sheaf of the target.
standard_prerequisites.use: The conclusion of the converse direction is exactly this condition, checked on modules (source lines 2290-2293, 2300-2303).

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial site and its total site
standard_prerequisites.statement: The total site of a simplicial site has as objects the objects of all levels, and the level morphisms g_n : C_n -> C_total are flat, with a_n = a composed with g_n.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the flatness of g_n used in the easy direction and the identification a_n = a composed with g_n used in the converse (source lines 2297-2300, 2320-2322).

standard_prerequisites.name: Inverse image of sheaves of modules along a composite
standard_prerequisites.statement: The inverse image along a composite of morphisms of topoi is the composite of the inverse images, so g_n^{-1} a^{-1} equals a_n^{-1} on structure sheaves.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the identification that turns the flatness hypothesis on a_n into the required injectivity (source lines 2320-2322).

core_obligations: Easy direction: using that each level morphism g_n is flat, conclude that a_n, being the composite of a with g_n, is flat whenever a is (source lines 2297-2300).

Set up the converse: suppose all a_n flat and reduce flatness of a to the injectivity of tensoring with the structure sheaf O over the inverse image of the structure sheaf of the target, applied to an injective map of modules (source lines 2300-2303).

Verify the injectivity at the level objects: evaluate on the objects of the total site, use the identification of g_n^{-1} a^{-1} with a_n^{-1} on structure sheaves, and invoke the assumed flatness of a_n to conclude the required injectivity (source lines 2304-2322).

proof_roadmap.step: If a is flat then each a_n is flat as a composite with g_n.
Conversely reduce flatness of a to injectivity of tensoring with O.
Evaluate at the level objects, identify the inverse images, and use flatness of a_n.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-flat-augmentation-modules at source lines 2285-2294: for the augmentation morphism a from the total site of a simplicial site to a fixed site, flatness of a is equivalent to flatness of each level morphism a_n. The proof at source lines 2296-2323 is a two-direction argument in which the forward direction is immediate from the flatness of the transition maps g_n but the converse needs real work. Assuming every a_n flat, one must show that the structure sheaf O is flat as a sheaf of modules over the inverse image of the structure sheaf of the target; this means taking an injective map of such modules and showing it stays injective after tensoring with O. The proof does this by evaluating at the objects of the total site, reducing to an expression in which the tensor product at an object of the n-th level is recognised, using the identification of the inverse image sheaves along the composite a_n = a composed with g_n, so that the assumed flatness of a_n gives the injectivity. The identification of the two inverse images is the point of the argument and the statement mentions neither it nor the reduction to the level objects. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
